chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: A looser band, with head arrangements
summary: The early band was relaxed and free, with many head arrangements and riffs worked up in the band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I think Freddie could say a little bit more about that, because inasmuch as it was probably a looser band than the subsequent ones. It was -- I mean the feeling is that later it becomes
somewhat more disciplined.
Mm -- oh yeah.
You could almost say it becomes a bit stiffer.
Right. Right.
I mean, at that time it seemed to be the idea -- loose floating.
Yes. It was. Definitely.
Yeah.
It was relaxed, and loose, and free, and easy. And, we just -- just swung -- you know, and like, there wasn't as much discipline, you know.
Well, I mean, there was -- the proportion of hits was much higher, wasn't it?
What?
The proportion of head arrangements was much higher?

Right. Definitely. You see it was easier to get along with most of the head things, and then the setting the riffs, and it was close. It was -- the feeling was -- you know. It was there all the time, and everybody was --
Everybody was getting into it.
-- everybody was doing their thing.
Yeah.
And, you could feel it. The audience could feel it, you know, and --
Yeah. Yeah. -- It was very thrilling.
Yes. It was.
So, really, everybody was like brothers?
Oh, listen. We were just like a -- (laugh).
Well, I think, you know -- another thing is that -- I think obviously when there are hits, and they're created within the band --
Yes.
-- it's very different than having Basie say to Andy Gibson or Jimmy Mundy--
Mm hmm.
-- write me an arrangement, you know.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
I mean, that isn't the same thing is it -- from somebody outside the band bringing an arrangement in?
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
Whereas you cook one up within the band -- it seems --
Which we did quite a bit.
